newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais withdraws legal suit.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais withdraws legal suit.

text.p: State-controlled Credit Lyonnais said on Thursday it had withdrawn a suit filed in the European Court of Justice contesting conditions imposed on it by the European Commission in exchange for approving last year's 45 billion franc government rescue of the French bank.
Bank chairman Jean Peyrelevade said the decision by the government to speed up privatisation of the bank had changed the situation and meant the suit filed earlier this year was no longer necessary.
The conservative government has said it wants to dispose of the bank as quickly as possible. It initially planned to sell it by around the year 2000.
In its suit, the bank had challenged the obligation imposed on it by the European Commission to dispose of 35 percent of its foreign assets in exchange for approving the 1995 bailout.
The bank's challenge followed a suit filed by rival French bank Societe Generale against the bailout.
Societe Generale had argued that the plan gave preferential treatment to Credit Lyonnais.
